### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.surround

### Neovim version

0.12.x

### Description

Here is my setup for mini.surround.

```lua
require("mini.surround").setup({
    mappings = {
        add = "ys",
        delete = "ds",
        find = "gl",
        find_left = "gs",
        highlight = "<leader>hs",
        replace = "cs",
    },
})
```

I had to change the default binds because the default 's' prefixed binding made the regular substitute command not work on Linux. (As an interesting aside, on Windows it would wait for `timeoutlen` and then run the default 's' behavior which is what I expected.) Anyway, I thought that the problem was with my rebinds so I deleted the options table so that the default binds would be set instead. The problem still persists.

Using the above code to illustrate behavior with '#' to denote cursor position:

## Example 1
### Before
```lua
require("mini.surround").setup({
    mappings = { -- Cursor position somewhere in between (but not on either of) these curly braces for "mappings"
        add = "ys",
        delete = "ds",
        find = "gl",
    #   find_left = "gs",
        highlight = "<leader>hs",
        replace = "cs",
    },
})
```
### Input
`sF{`
### After
```lua
require("mini.surround").setup({
    mappings = { -- Expecting to find it on this brace
       #add = "ys", -- But find it start of this line instead.
        delete = "ds",
        find = "gl",
        find_left = "gs",
        highlight = "<leader>hs",
        replace = "cs",
    },
})
```

## Example 2
### Before
```lua
require("mini.surround").setup({
    mappings = { -- Cursor position somewhere in between (but not on either of) these curly braces for "mappings"
        add = "ys",
        delete = "ds",
        find = "gl",
    #   find_left = "gs",
        highlight = "<leader>hs",
        replace = "cs",
    },
})
```
### Input
`sf{`
### After
```lua
require("mini.surround").setup({
    mappings = { -- Expecting to find it on this brace
        add = "ys",
        delete = "ds",
        find = "gl",
        find_left = "gs",
        highlight = "<leader>hs",
        replace = "cs"# -- But find it here (on top of the ',') instead.
    },
})
```

The behavior is as expected when using '}' instead of '{'. This behavior also occurs with other asymmetric bracket surrounding characters. I thought this might be intentional so that searching using the opening bracket would be similar to doing `t)` or `T(` instead of `f)` or `F(` respectively; however, that theory didn't seem to pan out because of the following example:

## Example 3
### Before
```lua
require("mini.sur#ound").setup({ -- Cursor position somewhere in between parentheses for `require` call.
    mappings = {
        add = "ys",
        delete = "ds",
        find = "gl",
        find_left = "gs",
        highlight = "<leader>hs",
        replace = "cs",
    },
})
```
### Input
`sF(`
### After
```lua
require#"mini.surround").setup({ -- On top of the open parenthesis instead of on opening double quote.
    mappings = { -- Expecting to find it on this brace
        add = "ys",
        delete = "ds",
        find = "gl",
        find_left = "gs",
        highlight = "<leader>hs",
        replace = "cs",
    },
})
```

The same behavior occurs if doing `sf(`, just to the right instead. If the opening bracket find functions were supposed to emulate a `t` or `T` command, I would expect to find this case to end with the cursor on the double quotes instead of on the bracket.

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

> The behavior is as expected when using '}' instead of '{'. This behavior also occurs with other asymmetric bracket surrounding characters. I thought this might be intentional so that searching using the opening bracket would be similar to doing `t)` or `T(` instead of `f)` or `F(` respectively; however, that theory didn't seem to pan out because of the following example:

Yes, this behavior is intentional and expected. It is a result of opening brackets surrounding id (`(`, `[`, `{`, `<`) [being treated differently](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-surround.html#minisurround-builtin-surroundings) from closing brackets surrounding is (`)`, `]`, `}`, `>`). In particular, opening brackets surroundings include whitespace that is adjacent from the inside to the found left and right surrounding. It also can include end-of-line character as a part of that whitespace.

You can see how they differ by highlighting `{` and `}` surroundings in all example cases (`<Leader>hs{` and `<Leader>hs}` with the setup from this issue). Executing `find_left` or `find` searches for edges of the surroundings to either left or right (possibly "wrapping around"). So in "Example 1":
- First `find_left` finds right edge of the left surrounding, which is the right end of the whitespace adjacent from the right to the `{`.
- Executing `find_left` again will move to the left edge of the left surrounding, which is `{`.
- Executing `find_left` again will move to the right edge of the right surrounding, which is `}`.
- Executing `find_left` again will move to the left edge of the right surrounding, which is the left end of the whitespace adjacent from the left to the `}`.

So the solution here is to navigate using closing brackets as surrounding id. Hope this helps.

---

> I had to change the default binds because the default 's' prefixed binding made the regular substitute command not work on Linux. (As an interesting aside, on Windows it would wait for `timeoutlen` and then run the default 's' behavior which is what I expected.)

If you mean `s` built-in key (that deletes a character at cursor and starts Insert mode), then it is indeed disabled inside of `require('mini.surround').setup()`. Which is [documented](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-surround.html#minisurround.config-mappings). This behavior does not depend on OS.

title: mini.surround find_left binding doesn't work quite right for left bracket characters
